newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher despite policy concerns.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher despite policy concerns.

text.p: Taiwan stocks closed higher on Tuesday despite concerns over the central bank's monetary policy, but brokers said the market was unlikely to reclaim the sizzle that added more than 1,000 points to the index already in 1997.
The weighted index closed 76.12 points, or 0.97 percent, higher at 7,956.57. Turnover was a hectic T$108.85 billion.
The central bank on Monday issued T$5 billion negotiable certificates of deposits to mop up excess liquidity in the banking system, and plans to issue T$3 biillion more on Tuesday.
The NCD issues followed a warning by central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung on Saturday that investors should exercise caution in the market's recent rally.
The index plunged by 1.29 percent on Monday over concerns that Hsu's comments and Monday's NCD issue may indicate that the central bank would tighten money policy to cool market sentiment.

"But the market's momentum turned out to be stronger than what many of us expected," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities. "The sentiment may be a bit more cautious, but it is not down."
Brokers said the central bank's caution drove investors to shares backed by sound fundamentals. Electronics, long considered Taiwan's strongest sector, gained 3.42 percent.

Major semiconductor firms all enjoyed strong buying -- with United Microelectronics gaining T$2.80 to T$47.40, Taiwan Semiconductor rising T$4 to T$67.50 and Mosel Vitelic closing T$2.30 higher at T$45.70.
The heavily weighted financials suffered mild profit-taking and fell by 0.44 percent.
"Financial shares would be most affected by a tightening of monetary policy," Fang said.
Brokers said they expected lingering uncertainty over the central bank's attitude to inject caution into the market for the short term. Immediate resistance was seen at 8,000 points.
A 7,900-8,000 trading range was seen for Wednesday.
